title: BPP episode_claim request (DESIGN.md §11.2, §16.6 item 3; registry R30 runtime)
description: Mutation (meta required, create-classed). The compare-and-swap on the ONE EpisodeLeaseHead: a successful claim increments the Byom fence, mints one immutable EpisodeAttempt, and commits the C2 ByomEpisodeBinding with BOTH fence epochs and the Δ5 context refs in the same transaction, idempotently over `stable_binding_key` (family contract L19–L22). `lease_ttl_seconds` mints the CLOCKED deadline (`now + ttl`): only an authoritatively expired or voluntarily yielded head is re-claimable — a crashed or silent worker enables nothing (D-RT-6/RT-10).

holder_runtime_binding.description: The workload identity claiming the lease (§14.7 runtime row).

lease_ttl_seconds.description: The proposed lease window; the deadline is minted as `now + lease_ttl_seconds` from the AUTHORITATIVE server clock. §11.2 fixes no window — this bundle pins 1..86400 (recorded deviation).

kovee_invocation_fence.description: The Kovee host-side fence: the other of the DUAL fences (family contract L21). A mutation carrying only one fence is invalid.

stable_binding_key.description: The L22 idempotent-create key of the ByomEpisodeBinding: an exact retry returns the identical row.

context_source_digest.description: Digest over the exact byom source-field fragment supplied to Kovee's ProviderContextManifest (§12.1, Δ5).

mandate_use_refs.description: MandateUse rows consumed for this Episode's authority (§13.2 tagging).

allowed_local_commitments.description: Closed set of Kovee local-commitment classes the hosted child may make intra-turn; anything else must go through call_open/pledge_propose/act_intent_* (family contract L34–L37).

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant with Z offset, semantically valid in the proleptic Gregorian calendar: the pattern pins the lexical ranges and implementations MUST additionally reject impossible calendar instants (e.g. 2026-02-30) — the conformance runner enforces this on every vector; leap seconds are not accepted. DESIGN.md does not fix a timestamp wire encoding; this derivation freezes with the bundle (gap note G3, amended per RT-17).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef: every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Wire shape, class/algorithm pairing, and key_ref presence per the ratified family profile.

mutationMeta.description: MutationMeta (§14.2), create-classed: this operation creates a record (or CASes a subordinate head through its own body fields), so the closed create meta carries NO expected_revision member — supplying one fails the closed schema (RT-01: update CAS is structural, never optional).

oneOf.$comment: Both optional Δ5 context pairs present.

Neither optional pair; ref/digest pairs are all-or-none.

$comment: The Δ5 pairs mirror the frozen spec/governed-work/byom-episode-binding.schema.json oneOf exactly: a half pair is refused by the shape, not by code.
